findings.title: Unauthenticated /qto-extract webhook → Execute Command RCE via model_path + arbitrary file write
findings.description: BIM QTO n8n workflow triggers on webhook path /qto-extract with no authentication. First step Execute Command interpolates attacker-controlled {{$json.model_path}} into a shell command. Final step Write Binary File uses attacker-controlled {{$json.output_path}}. Distinct from already-known localFileTrigger executeCommand on BIM Change Detection (folder watch), because here the source is a public HTTP webhook.
findings.impact: Remote code execution on the n8n host as the n8n process user; arbitrary file write via output_path.
findings.attack_path:
1. Deploy ifc-qto-extraction n8n Integration as written.
2. POST /webhook/qto-extract with model_path ending in quote-breakout: C:\tmp\x.rvt" & whoami > C:\tmp\qto_rce.txt & rem "
3. Execute Command expands to RvtExporter.exe "..." & whoami ... → shell runs attacker command.
4. Optionally set output_path to traverse and overwrite an arbitrary path.
findings.remediation: Require webhook auth (header/HMAC). Never interpolate user input into Execute Command; pass argv-safe fixed converter invocation. Constrain output_path under an allowlisted directory.

findings.title: Unauthenticated daily-report-data webhook drives Procore OAuth fetch, email, and SharePoint write
findings.description: Webhook Input POST path daily-report-data has no authentication. Python helper posts project_id, project_name, site_lat/lon, and distribution_list. Get Site Photos calls Procore with OAuth using {{$json.project_id}}. Send Email uses toEmail={{$json.distribution_list}}. SharePoint uploads the generated report. Attacker can poison official daily reports and abuse the Procore token; when distribution_list is taken from the webhook payload as the helper + emailSend node indicate, attacker also receives the PDF.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated abuse of Procore OAuth credentials; forged/poisoned daily construction reports emailed and stored on SharePoint; possible recipient takeover via distribution_list.
findings.attack_path:
1. Discover n8n webhook URL /webhook/daily-report-data.
2. POST project_id of a sensitive Procore project + distribution_list=attacker@evil.
3. Workflow OAuth-fetches that project's images, builds PDF, emails distribution_list, uploads SharePoint.
findings.remediation: Authenticate webhook; hardcode distribution list from env/credentials; map project_id through an allowlist; do not accept recipient addresses from the request body.

findings.title: Unauthenticated photo-upload webhook writes official Airtable Site Photos and burns Anthropic key
findings.description: Photo Webhook POST path photo-upload has no authentication, accepts binary/base64 uploads, sends them to Anthropic with company API key, then Airtable create into Site Photos. Scheduled report emails safety issues derived from those rows to PHOTO_REPORT_RECIPIENTS.
findings.impact: Anyone who can hit the webhook can insert forged site/safety records into the official photo log and force Anthropic spend; poisoned safety issues appear in stakeholder email reports.
findings.attack_path:
1. POST /webhook/photo-upload with attacker image + filename.
2. Claude Vision analyzes; Parse AI Response builds fields.
3. Airtable create stores official Site Photos row.
4. Evening schedule emails safety_issues from those rows.
findings.remediation: Authenticate webhook; restrict uploads to known field devices/accounts; validate/quarantine before Airtable write.

findings.title: Telegram field bot has no user allowlist; arbitrary users create official reports
findings.description: n8n workflow Telegram Trigger → PostgreSQL insert with no auth gate. Python Application registers CommandHandler/MessageHandler for all users; handle_photo/handle_text accept any from_user.id and log reports. generate_daily_report SELECTs telegram_reports into the official daily summary. No ALLOWED_USER_IDS / chat allowlist appears in the deployable sample.
findings.impact: Anyone who finds the public bot can inject photos/text into official field records and daily summaries.
findings.attack_path:
1. Discover bot username from BotFather naming pattern / leaked token surface.
2. Send photo or text report.
3. n8n inserts into PostgreSQL / Python logs report.
4. generate_daily_report aggregates into official daily summary.
findings.remediation: Enforce allowlisted Telegram user IDs / chat IDs before any DB write; require /start invite tokens issued by PMs.

findings.title: Open Telegram /start self-registration as Foreman with no allowlist
findings.description: Workflow routes /start. Documented registration asks for name and self-selected role including Прораб (Foreman), then completes registration and stores Telegram ID. Workers sheet Telegram_ID is defined as User ID from /start. No invite code, admin approval, or allowlist is specified. Registered IDs become the roster PMs use for Executor_ID task assignment and official status/photo responses.
findings.impact: Attacker joins the official Workers roster as Foreman, enabling assignment of real tasks, receipt of project details, and submission of official completion/photo/GPS records.
findings.attack_path:
1. Message bot /start.
2. Provide name; choose role Прораб.
3. Bot confirms registration with attacker Telegram ID.
4. ID appears in Workers; PM assigns Executor_ID; attacker receives tasks and can submit official responses/photos.
findings.remediation: Disable open /start roster writes; require PM-provisioned invite tokens or pre-seeded allowlisted Telegram IDs before role assignment.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /rfi-notification webhook emails and Telegrams staff from attacker fields
findings.description: Webhook path /rfi-notification has no authentication. Attacker supplies rfi_number, subject, assigned_to, priority, due date. Workflow looks up Contacts by role={{assigned_to}}, then Emails and Telegrams those recipients. Subject is interpolated into the email Subject header (CRLF header-injection risk) and Telegram body.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated phishing/spam to project contacts; forged RFI urgency; possible email header injection via subject.
findings.attack_path:
1. POST /webhook/rfi-notification with assigned_to matching a Contacts role (e.g. Architect) and attacker-controlled subject.
2. Workflow resolves emails/telegram_ids from Contacts.
3. Staff receive forged RFI email + Telegram.
findings.remediation: Authenticate webhook; strip CRLF from subject; do not let untrusted callers choose assigned_to roles that fan out notifications.
